clue.text: Yard's tracking call that's bogus

indicators.note: something tracking another follows behind it, so the yard abbreviation comes after the call

parts.note: to call someone is to phone them
Y is an abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: Scotland Yard traces a hoax phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard' suggests Scotland Yard, the London police headquarters, but it is only the unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: Something phoney is fake or counterfeit, a synonym of bogus.

clue.text: Run down clue for heaps?

parts.note: a gradual winding down or discontinuation of something
read as a clue in its own right: the first word is a rearrangement of the letters of heaps, and the second word tells you to rearrange them

explanation.surface: A setter jokes that a wind-down could clue a pile of things.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer works backwards as a clue: its first part is the letters of HEAPS, and its second part is an anagram signal, so the whole answer would clue HEAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A phase-out is the gradual ending of a scheme or product, a running down of it.

clue.text: Secretly working and scheming to pen article

indicators.note: to pen something is to shut it in, so the article sits enclosed between the other pieces

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
the definite article
sly means crafty or scheming

explanation.surface: Someone works covertly, plotting to write a piece for a paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working and scheming' together make the outer pair, which pens the article between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the sly means doing it covertly, without others knowing.

clue.text: With game time disappearing, happy to equalise

indicators.note: something disappearing is lost, so the letter for time drops out of the word for game

parts.note: a sporting event is a game or contest
T is the abbreviation for time
to feel up is to be cheerful

explanation.surface: As the clock runs down in a match, a team is glad to draw level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game time' reads as one phrase about the clock, but game and time are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To even up is to make level or equal, the same as to equalise.

clue.text: Yelps fit to bust in misery

indicators.note: something bust is broken apart, so the letters are smashed and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone yelps fit to burst in their misery.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-pity is a wallowing unhappiness about one's own lot, a form of misery.

clue.text: Make engravings in France and Switzerland

indicators.note: in France tells you to translate the linking word into French

parts.note: et is French for and
CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: An engraver works in two European countries.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to engrave a design, usually by eating into metal with acid.

clue.text: Rocket maybe needs industry to support launch

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece lies beneath, so industry comes after launch

parts.note: to fire is to launch a missile
industry in the sense of diligent work

explanation.surface: Getting a rocket off the ground needs industrial effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket is one example of a firework, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Popular model of car incorporates air conditioner for baby

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take something into the body of another, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a fan cools the air
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A popular car model comes with air conditioning, good for a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant is a very young child, a baby.

clue.text: Shouted young students crossing rising river

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means reading upwards, so the river's name is turned around

parts.note: Y is an abbreviation for young

indicators.note: the students are crossing the river, so they sit within it

parts.note: the River Dee read upwards
L is a learner driver; two of them make students

explanation.surface: Young students wading across a swollen river shouted out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a British river; turned round it holds the two learners.
explanation.definitionFit: Yelled is the past tense of yell, to cry out loudly, so it means shouted.

clue.text: Bible's covered with real carved horn

indicators.note: one thing covered with another is wrapped inside it
something carved is cut into a new shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
NT is the New Testament, part of the Bible

explanation.surface: A Bible bound in genuine carved horn.
explanation.definitionFit: An antler is the branched bony horn of a deer.

clue.text: Occasionally Ford Consul generated sneering

indicators.note: generated means produced afresh, so the letters are made into a new word
occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of the car maker is kept

parts.note: first and third letters of the name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Ford Consul, an old family car, sometimes drew contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ford Consul was a 1950s British saloon; it looks like one name but only the first word is thinned.
explanation.definitionFit: Scornful describes someone showing contempt, which is what sneering expresses.

clue.text: After 12 most of old fellows fall asleep

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter, so the final letter is cut
after tells you the old fellows come behind the trimmed number in the answer

parts.note: twelve is a dozen
O is an abbreviation for old
F is fellow; doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: After midnight, most of the old men nod off.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but it is just the number twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: To doze off is to drift into sleep, an idiom for falling asleep.

clue.text: Endlessly vexed copper with nonsense about will administrator

indicators.note: without ends means both the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: the word with its outer letters lopped
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the word for nonsense runs backwards

parts.note: rot means rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: An irritated policeman talks nonsense to the person handling a will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer, but here it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An executor is the person named to carry out the terms of a will.

clue.text: Suggestion involving wife causes pain

indicators.note: to involve something is to include it within, so wife goes inside

parts.note: a tinge is a slight trace or suggestion
W is an abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A hint about the wife is upsetting.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinge is a sudden sharp pang, a brief pain.

clue.text: Killer whale repelled hit with flipper?

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so the word for killer whale runs backwards

parts.note: the orca is the killer whale
to bat a ball is to hit it

explanation.surface: A killer whale was driven off by a blow from a seal's flipper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipper' makes you think of a sea creature's limb, which suits the whale; the question mark flags someone who does flips.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat performs somersaults and flips, so is whimsically a flipper.

clue.text: Dreadful lurgy, with no resistance, is frightful

indicators.note: dreadful means in a terrible state, so the letters are jumbled
with no means lacking, so the letter for resistance is taken away

parts.note: lurgy is British slang for an unspecified illness
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A nasty bug that you cannot fight off is horrible.
explanation.walkthrough: The lurgy is jokey British slang for a vague infectious illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly can mean unpleasant or hideous, which is what frightful means here.

clue.text: Sending off has Derby County, initially behind, clamping down

indicators.note: to clamp is to grip from both sides, so behind encloses the club's initials

parts.note: the rear is the behind

indicators.note: initially points to the first letters of the football club's two names

parts.note: first letters of the two words
D is the abbreviation for down, as in clue references

explanation.surface: A sending-off leaves Derby County behind and tightening up their defence.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby County is an English football club, which pulls the eye to football; the referee shows a red card when sending a player off.
explanation.definitionFit: A red card is shown to a player being dismissed, so it stands for a sending-off.

clue.text: Important the Spanish graduate's university has place to go climbing

indicators.note: in a down answer, climbing means reading upwards, so the whole string is turned round

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate
U is an abbreviation for university
the lav is the toilet, a place to go

explanation.surface: A Spanish graduate's university has a key climbing site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place to go' is a euphemism for a toilet; lav is short for lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Something valuable is of great worth or importance.

clue.text: Became hysterical when Dad's arrested

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
nicked is British slang for arrested

explanation.surface: Someone lost it when their father was taken in by police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dad's' here means 'Dad has', joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To panic is to be overcome by sudden fear, so panicked means became hysterical.

clue.text: Lloyd is a reformed subversive

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters take a new shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Lloyd is a former rebel who has mended his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 'a' belongs to the letters, though it reads as an article before 'reformed subversive'.
explanation.definitionFit: Subversive means undermining authority, which is the act of someone disloyal.

clue.text: Spice Girls finale's special for fan

indicators.note: the finale is the closing part, so only the last letter of girls is kept

parts.note: last letter

indicators.note: special as in specially made, so the letters are freshly arranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Spice Girls' last show was a treat for a devoted follower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spice Girls' reads as the pop group, but 'Spice' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron is a costly yellow spice made from crocus stigmas.

clue.text: Long skirt has greatest impact head-on

parts.note: max is short for maximum, the greatest

indicators.note: the head is the front, so only the first letter of impact is used

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: A floor-length skirt makes the biggest splash when seen from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxi is a skirt or dress reaching to the ankles.

clue.text: Abruptly spring up chasing dog with bird

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so this piece comes after the dog

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means reading upwards, so the trimmed word is turned round
abruptly means cut off short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a spring is a source of water, a well

explanation.surface: A dog leaps up suddenly and chases a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring up' reads as leaping, but spring is the water source and up is a separate signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The curlew is a wading bird with a long down-curved bill.

clue.text: Mysterious husband has study filled with papers

indicators.note: something filled with another holds it inside

parts.note: H is an abbreviation for husband
ID means identity papers
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A man's study is strangely stuffed with documents.
explanation.walkthrough: The papers go inside the husband-plus-study pair, between the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden can mean concealed or obscure in meaning, close to mysterious.

clue.text: Shown inside, doffed orange hat

indicators.note: shown inside means the letters appear within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Indoors, someone took off an orange hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat with a creased crown.

clue.text: High class equine, clipped and groomed, is one of a kind

parts.note: U means upper-class

indicators.note: groomed means tidied and rearranged, so the letters are put in a new order
clipped means trimmed short, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A thoroughbred horse, trimmed and brushed, is unlike any other.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is a British usage, as in the old 'U and non-U' speech labels.
explanation.definitionFit: Unique means being the only one of its kind.

clue.text: Friend's broadcast backed liberal stuff

parts.note: a mate is a friend

indicators.note: backed means moved backwards, so the word for broadcast runs the other way

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
L is an abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A friend's programme supported progressive content.
explanation.definitionFit: Material and stuff both mean the substance or fabric something is made of.

clue.text: Deliver father's tablets

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
E is ecstasy, a drug taken as a tablet; two for the plural

explanation.surface: Bring a father his pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'father's' means 'father has', joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone from danger is to free or rescue them.

clue.text: Woman's right to cut offer for Beetle

parts.note: a lady is a woman

indicators.note: something cutting another slices into it, so the letter sits inside

parts.note: a bid is an offer at auction
R is an abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A woman has the right to undercut an offer for a VW Beetle car.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on 'Beetle' hints at the Volkswagen, but it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladybird is a small spotted beetle, called a ladybug in America.

clue.text: Horsewoman has about a thousand invested in jumper

indicators.note: money invested in something is put into it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a joey is a young kangaroo, a jumper
c is short for circa, about
K stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: A rider has about a thousand pounds put into a showjumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a horse or a sweater, but it is a baby kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: A jockey is a professional rider in horse races; a horsewoman can be one.

clue.text: Thought to have claimed victory days before invading

parts.note: to have won is to have claimed victory

indicators.note: an invader goes inside territory, so before is placed within days

parts.note: D is days; doubled for the plural
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone believed they had won days before an invasion.
explanation.definitionFit: To wonder is to ponder or think about something, so wondered means thought.

clue.text: Hooligan's vehicle knocked over boy

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so the word for boy runs backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A yob's van ran down a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooligan's' means 'Hooligan has', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal deliberately damages property, the sort of thing a hooligan does.
